zoom_levels_observed: wide / full-body (walking away, back to camera)
phone-screen insert (camera pointed at his own handset)
framing_style.description: Single-source handheld selfie vlog, one continuous shoot (office corridor then a sporting-goods store), camera held at arm's length in the subject's own hand. There is NO programmatic crop ramp: ORB+RANSAC similarity fits across all 16 shots give per-shot cumulative scale between 0.82x and 1.49x with the sign changing shot to shot (-16.1%/s to +43.9%/s) and non-monotonic within shots - that is the arm physically moving, not an editor's zoom. The one exception is a hard punch-in CUT at 18.850s: scale 0.888 across the cut (+12.6% instant zoom on the same phone-screen footage) while the same measurement inside the shots either side is 1.002 and 1.008. Motion is violent whip-panning throughout: mean per-frame masked MAD is 12.2/255 with the camera swinging through 90 degrees within single shots, and the final 3.37s shot is a walking tracking shot following him down an aisle. Subject vertical position: face/eyeline sits high, roughly 12-30% of frame height in the medium default framing (extreme close-ups fill 0-60%), leaving the caption at 53% clear below him. Cuts almost always jump to different footage - 14 of 15 land on a different pose, angle or location; only the 18.850s cut reframes the same footage.

caption.position: 53% of frame height (block centre for a 1-line card; measured full-res bbox y=734-791 of 1440 = 51.0-54.9%, centre 52.9%). 2-line cards keep line 1 at ~52% and add line 2 at ~58-59%, line pitch ~6% of H (~86px). Horizontally centred (measured cx=547.5 vs frame centre 540). The outro card from 26.9s sits lower at ~62.5%.
caption.style_description: Heavy geometric sans, ExtraBold, ALL CAPS, cap height 58px at 1080x1440 (4.0% of frame height), 1-2 lines, cards run 1-6 words (typical 3-4) and are built WORD BY WORD - each new word scale-pops in while the earlier words stay put, then the whole card cuts away and the next card starts. Word-level colouring is the signature: base white, with the emphasised word(s) in a saturated accent, and a handful of words rendered per-LETTER in multiple colours (e.g. PORTUGAL runs orange/yellow/green). A few emphasised words also get a filled rounded colour box behind them (GUYS on green, SECRET on red, MOUTH SHUT on purple).
caption.color: white base; accent words in red (~#FF4D4D), cyan (~#4FC3F7), green (~#7CE83C), violet (~#8A6EF0), orange and yellow; some words per-letter multicoloured
caption.outline: no hard stroke - a soft dark drop-shadow/glow hugging the glyphs (roughly 4-8px blurred black at ~50% opacity, tinted toward the glyph colour on coloured words). Reads as a shadow, not an outline.
caption.animation: Per-word scale-in ramp, anchored bottom-centre, no overshoot. Measured on the single-word card CRAZY (full-res cyan bbox, frames 64-90): word absent through n=65, first appears n=66 at width 93px, then 130/158/180/198/214/228/236/248/256/260/266 to a settled 272px. As a fraction of settled size: 0.34 (n=66), 0.48, 0.58, 0.66, 0.73, 0.79, 0.84, 0.87, 0.91, 0.94, 0.96, 0.98 (n=77), 1.00 by n=78-80. So start scale 0.34x, peak scale 1.00x (peak IS the settle - monotonic ease-out, no elastic overshoot), settles 12-14 frames after entry = 200-233ms. The bbox bottom edge stays pinned at y=791 while the top rises 772 -> 734 and cx stays 547.5, so the transform origin is bottom-centre. This is a PER-WORD pop, not a full-frame scale ramp: verified on the 2-line card FIFA ACTUALLY / JUST ANNOUNCED IT (n=540-576, gridlines at 45/50/55/60% overlaid) where the already-placed words and both line baselines stay pixel-locked while only the newly added word scales in; a composite-wide ramp would have moved every line and the video under it.

effects: coloured full-frame flash transitions: solid cyan at 15.933s and solid white-with-RGB-split at 26.633s, both covering a real cut; each is one saturated frame then a ~0.2-0.35s decay back to picture
solid green full-frame flash at 17.133s that does NOT cover a cut - same phone footage before and after; it is an emphasis hit that marks the red circle appearing
composited PNG graphic overlay: gold FIFA World Cup trophy with 'FIFA' wordmark, sat over his chest ~8.8-9.8s (needs a second filtergraph input)
drawn red circle annotation ringing the face inside the Instagram post on the phone screen, ~17.3-18.9s
large freeze-face emoji sticker, ~220px tall (15% of frame height), horizontally centred, at ~73-88% of frame height, present from ~26.9s to the end
per-word coloured caption fills, per-letter multicolour on some words, filled rounded colour boxes behind selected words
chromatic/RGB-split vertical smear inside the white flash frames (26.633-26.72s)
stutter/strobe passage 24.65-25.70s: motion-compensated frame-to-frame residual alternates ~5 then ~35, i.e. picture effectively updates at 30Hz for ~1.05s
NOT present: borders, grain, vignette, progress bar, zoom/speed lines, meme cutaway, background removal, arrows
hook: No cut for the first 2.833s. Opens mid-scream: extreme close-up of the subject, head thrown back laughing/yelling at arm's length in a bare office corridor, camera whipping. The caption builds word by word from t=0.15s - 'CHAT,' then 'TODAY' (red) 'GOING TO BE A' - and at 1.100s the card cuts to a single cyan 'CRAZY' that scale-pops in over 200ms. He then backs away down the corridor into a wide full-body shot while 'DAY' and 'BRO' land. Pure energy and a promise of news; no title card, no b-roll, no visual gag.
audio: Integrated -7.4 LUFS, LRA 2.7 LU, true peak +1.5 dBFS (1269 samples of 480208 at digital full scale - it is clipped). Raw single-source location audio only: his shouted voice plus store/corridor ambience, hard-limited and loudness-maximised. NO music bed - 0.1s RMS drops to -29.6 dBFS in the pauses at 1.7s, 8.3s and 25.9s against a -10.3 dBFS median, and the quiet-window spectrum is 200Hz-4kHz room tone with almost nothing below 200Hz, so nothing is holding the floor up. Possible short transition SFX on cuts: 3-8kHz energy rises across the cut in 7 of the 15 cuts by more than the p90 of 200 random non-cut times (+22.7dB at 20.117s, +14.0 at 26.633s, +13.0 at 10.017s), but the constant shouting makes this suggestive rather than proven.
notes: COMPLETE. Method. (1) 30-in-60 check: no duplicated frames anywhere. Raw consecutive MAD never falls below 0.35/255 (0 of 1799 pairs) and even-lag vs odd-lag means are 12.21 vs 12.74. Re-tested properly with motion compensation (phaseCorrelate shift then residual MAD) over six 60-frame regions spread across the clip: residuals 9-11 with no even/odd split anywhere except 24.7-25.7s. Genuine 60fps; cut times do NOT land on a 30fps grid (e.g. 6.267s = frame 376, odd). (2) Cut detection: ffmpeg's scene filter was unusable here - it returned 148 hits at 0.10 and 31 at 0.20 (files scenes_0.10.txt / scenes_0.20.txt from the earlier session), including 60+ consecutive hits inside a single shaky shot. Instead: per-frame mean-absolute-difference on 135x180 grayscale with rows 30-70% of frame height masked out (the caption band, located by looking - captions sit at 51-65% and the emoji reaches 88%), then divided by a local median over a +/-40 frame window to normalise for this clip's very high motion baseline. Candidates at ratio>2.0 and MAD>25 gave 21 groups; the threshold was then dropped to ratio>1.55 / MAD>20 to catch anything hiding in high-motion passages, giving 27 more. All 48 were verified on labelled before/after pairs extracted with select='eq(n,K)' (v2/pairsheet_1..6.png, v2/uncert_1..4.png) - never with -ss. 15 survived. (3) What was rejected and why: caption-card swaps and word additions fire the metric but the picture is identical either side - rejected at 1.000s, 1.533s, 2.400s, 4.517s, 5.400s, 7.083s, 12.267s, 14.917s, 22.283s, 22.983s, 23.250s. Subject-motion plateaus rejected at 19.867s, 22.483s, 24.067s, 24.267s. A sustained high-difference run at 24.77-25.67s was 30 alternating-frame spikes, not 30 cuts - the stutter passage, rejected wholesale. Separation was not as clean as the sibling clip: real cuts scored 30.6-78.1 masked MAD against a 10.4 median and 19.7 p90, so the 20-30 band is genuinely ambiguous and was settled by eye on frame pairs, not by threshold. (4) The green flash at 17.133s scored MAD 69.4 - higher than most real cuts - but the phone footage before and after is the same shot, so it is counted as an effect, not a cut; a threshold-only pass would have added a 16th cut here. (5) The apparent scale ramp inside shots is camera, not crop - see framing_style.description. (6) Nothing here needs more than one source video plus overlays: the phone-screen section is filmed, not composited, but the trophy PNG, the red circle and the emoji sticker each need an extra filtergraph input. (7) Unresolved: the 24.65-25.70s stutter. ORB returns exactly repeated integer translations there (+6.000, -3.800, -7.100 px at 270x360) which looks synthetic, but the frames also show extreme whip-pan blur that could produce the same signature; I could not separate an applied shake/stutter filter from real camera whip and have described the measurement rather than picking one. (8) words_per_card 3.5 is the mean of the fully-built cards read off the contact sheets (range 1-6); it is a read count, not an automated one. (9) Deliverables reused from the earlier session: none of its conclusions (there were none) and none of its unlabelled sheets; scenes_*.txt were read only to document that the scene filter fails on this clip. All figures above come from v2/ artifacts built in this pass.
